answer: Give every new agent a dawn opal bond: it locks a refundable stake in escrow before its first paid job and takes only small jobs. Each finished job earns a non-transferable mark, and three clean marks release one slice while the rest stays locked until the agent reaches the zenith of a proven record. A fake caught cheating loses its stake and marks, so a fresh identity starts from zero. Assume here each fake costs $1,500 to fund, about $1.5 million for 1,000 fakes. Like a harbour that trusts only storm-tested captains, the economy rewards earned history, not cheap copies.
